units.function: Builds the npm CLI as one Node 20 ESM bundle, embedding selected workspace packages and dependencies while leaving the server and most third-party packages external.
units.dependencyDirection: Build config -> repository package manifests and bundled-dependency policy -> esbuild resolution. It encodes deployment topology through source-tree paths.
units.keyDataModels: workspace path allowlist, external workspace set, generated bundled npm dependency set and embedded-postgres optional native dependencies.
units.lifecycle: Read manifests -> collect external dependency names -> resolve embedded PostgreSQL optional packages -> bundle src/index.ts with source map and shebang.
units.testAssessment: No focused test directly executes this build configuration. Packaging scripts/tests are separate pending units; the current CLI no-emit TypeScript check does not prove bundle completeness, installability, license notices, native portability or runtime dynamic imports.
units.designRationale: Ship one convenient CLI artifact while keeping the separately published server replaceable at runtime and preserving native optional dependency installation.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs reproducible, attestable CLI/service/Connector artifacts with explicit module ownership, SBOM/license output and independent deployment profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY for the embedded-versus-external inventory idea. Company OS should generate bundle policy from package ownership metadata and verify artifacts, licenses, native targets and dynamic boundaries in CI.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct domain conflict; opaque bundling can obscure which Connector/runtime code is authorized in an operator artifact.
evidence: git history includes fc5a30805ed3c95ac6598c8660261a018b5b5a7f, d31a28828b82c292adc61d728f00e89c4b494da3, fd2f82ac5bba6ce2db0c5d17c573733af5f2bbb8 and 73eb23734f25c570d88665e672f80d740797c632
units.securityFindings: Workspace paths and bundled dependency policy are manually duplicated, so new packages can drift between artifact and manifest behavior. No metafile/SBOM/license notice, integrity/signing/reproducibility assertion or bundle smoke test appears here. Source maps ship with the artifact; native optional dependency coverage is inferred from a local installed package manifest.

units.function: The executable CLI composition root registering setup, deployment, identity, data, Agent, work, approval, Plugin, Connector-like, maintenance and worktree commands plus global pre-action context/env/telemetry hooks and top-level error handling.
units.dependencyDirection: Single CLI entrypoint -> every command family, config/env, telemetry and install/service lifecycle. It is a broad composition root but also embeds policy defaults and ambient target selection.
units.keyDataModels: Commander command tree; data-dir/config/context/profile/API key options; run repair/force defaults; bootstrap CEO options; process exit status.
units.lifecycle: Construct command tree -> before every action mutate target context, load dotenv and initialize telemetry -> invoke selected command -> catch and print message -> always flush singleton telemetry -> exit on caught failure.
units.testAssessment: Many completed parity/command suites prove registration and route spelling, and CLI TypeScript passes. No focused main/preAction/flush/error test proves mixed config precedence, invalid config, telemetry failure, signal handling, stable error codes, Secret argv exposure or every destructive command's effect classification.
units.designRationale: A single discoverable executable and common pre-action hook keep a large operator surface convenient and consistent.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a generated/thin operator CLI over stable APIs with explicit DeploymentContext, effect classes, machine-stable errors, accountable confirmations and no duplicate authority model.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a thin composition shell generated from canonical command/API contracts. Resolve immutable target/auth context first, classify effects, bind destructive plans to approvals, redact outputs and keep telemetry independent from command success.
units.responsibilityConflict: Run defaults to repair, force/yes flags bypass safeguards, bootstrap uses CEO as identity authority, and high-impact operations share the same ambient context without an accountable-human change envelope.
evidence: Completed CLI parity/command evidence reused; CLI TypeScript passes
units.securityFindings: HIGH: --api-key accepts bearer material in process argv. HIGH: the global pre-action uses ambient mutable config/env, including the cross-instance Secret issue from the completed env audit. Errors are English strings with no stable code and may contain paths/source details. flushTelemetry failure can replace command outcome or escape the catch because it runs in finally; void main has no outer rejection handler. There is no signal-aware flush/cleanup. Broad static imports also make every Adapter/data/deployment capability part of one privileged operator process.

units.function: Declares the public MIT paperclipai executable package, scripts and a runtime dependency graph spanning database, server, shared code and ten vendor/runtime Adapter packages.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI package -> Paperclip server/database/shared plus all listed vendor/local/gateway Adapters and third-party process/storage/config libraries.
units.keyDataModels: npm package identity/version/bin/files/license and workspace dependency inventory.
units.lifecycle: Development executes TS directly; release bundles then chmods one dist entry; npm publishes only dist while dependencies remain manifest runtime requirements.
units.testAssessment: Manifest validity is indirectly exercised by install/build tooling, but this unit has no direct contract test for published tarball contents, licenses/SBOM, dependency pin consistency, optional native behavior or clean-install execution.
units.designRationale: Offer an all-in-one operator distribution capable of local Agent runtimes and dynamic server startup.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires vendor-neutral core packages and separately permissioned Connector adapters so installing control-plane tooling does not grant every vendor runtime dependency.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT this package topology. Keep Company OS CLI/API contracts separate from server, database implementation and vendor Connector packages; publish an explicit minimal core plus opt-in signed Connectors.
units.responsibilityConflict: A single privileged package collapses operator, database, server and vendor execution trust domains and cannot express per-Connector installation approval/capability custody.
evidence: package declares MIT; repository license/provenance obligations remain governed by the pinned audit
dependency history includes f9034ab3ca8b9b3be011de94b9c82f1e6322dae9, db61cc97d3a369db6a3f54d9e6e97040fd6b4b90, 753544d704699c2d1db19a55798a6795fe3767a1 and eedc7ddef27e852ab130c8f5c68149ff86bec17f
units.securityFindings: The CLI runtime dependency surface includes database, server and every listed Adapter, increasing supply-chain and privilege blast radius. Workspace ranges are replaced during publication by separate tooling, so this manifest alone does not prove exact shipped versions. clean uses recursive deletion but only a fixed dist target. No scripts entry provides tests or published-artifact verification.

units.function: Initializes a process-singleton shared telemetry client from file config, stores instance state and re-exports three lifecycle event helpers.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI telemetry facade -> relative shared telemetry source -> config store, ambient instance root and network client.
units.keyDataModels: enabled setting, singleton client, instance telemetry state, CLI version and install/import events.
units.lifecycle: Read config -> resolve enabled policy -> lazily create client/state -> reuse forever -> enqueue events elsewhere -> flush at CLI completion.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed telemetry evidence: 2/2 passed for explicit opt-out and lazy state creation. Default/invalid config, consent, endpoint/payload, PII/Secret redaction, identifier rotation, retries/limits, deletion/export, proxies/TLS and failure effects are absent.
units.designRationale: Centralize low-friction anonymous lifecycle telemetry while avoiding state creation when explicitly disabled.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs deployment-profile-specific observability and optional product analytics with explicit enterprise policy, data classification, regional routing and failure isolation.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT through ObservabilityPort and separately consented ProductAnalyticsPort. Resolve policy per immutable deployment context; invalid/unreadable config must fail closed for analytics, and telemetry failure must never change command result.
units.responsibilityConflict: Company data/import signals cannot be exported based on an implicit default without a responsible organization policy and auditable data-processing basis.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL privacy fail-open: initTelemetryFromConfigFile catches any config read/validation failure and calls initTelemetry() with default policy, so a corrupted config that intended opt-out can enable analytics. The singleton is not keyed by config/instance and can retain the first target across embedded multi-instance use; its state directory is ambient rather than derived from configPath. Shared telemetry internals remain independently audited.

units.function: Extends the repository TypeScript baseline and expands the CLI compilation root to shared and plugin-creator source trees.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI compiler project -> repository base config and sibling package source directories.
units.keyDataModels: Compiler root/out directories and included source sets.
units.testAssessment: CLI no-emit TypeScript passes at the pinned source. This proves type consistency under the monorepo layout, not published package isolation or runtime boundaries.
units.designRationale: Allow direct monorepo source imports to typecheck and emit under one root.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs enforceable package/project boundaries and independent buildability for core, adapters, SDK, Web and deployment tooling.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT as a boundary model. Use project references/package exports plus dependency guards so the CLI cannot compile against sibling internals accidentally.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct product conflict; weak compile boundaries permit identity/data/runtime types to leak into privileged tooling.
units.securityFindings: Including sibling source trees formalizes monorepo source coupling rather than public contracts. The actual strictness/options belong to the separately auditable base config.

units.function: Resolves the CLI package version and enriches it with managed-install source/channel/ref/SHA and payload-path provenance when the executing file matches the active manifest.
units.dependencyDirection: Version helper -> package.json plus managed install-store manifest/path verification.
units.keyDataModels: package version, install source/ref/SHA/channel, payload path and executable identity.
units.lifecycle: Load package version -> read install manifest -> verify executable belongs to active payload -> render provenance -> fail back to package version.
units.testAssessment: Existing managed-install tests exercise provenance output as part of 16/16 passing install cases. Malformed manifests and store behavior are covered separately; version fallback observability and information disclosure are not directly isolated.
units.designRationale: Make operator bug reports and rollback decisions traceable to the actual managed payload rather than only its semantic package version.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs verifiable build/release/Connector provenance in diagnostics and runtime attestation.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the active-executable-to-manifest binding and source revision display. Return structured BuildIdentity and expose only a redacted artifact ID by default; verify signatures/SBOM/digest upstream.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct conflict; provenance should be included in execution/evidence attestations rather than being terminal decoration only.
evidence: Existing application:cli/__tests__/install-command assessment: 16/16 passed and provenance asserted
units.securityFindings: Positive: provenance is shown only after active executable verification. The absolute payload path is disclosed in version output and all resolution failures silently degrade to package version, hiding tamper/corruption from operators. Ref/SHA authenticity depends on the install-store supply-chain controls audited separately.

units.function: Selects Vitest's Node environment with all other behavior inherited from defaults.
units.testAssessment: The repository contains many focused CLI tests, but this config enforces no coverage threshold, explicit include/exclude, serial-resource policy, timeout, cleanup leak detection or environment isolation. Several completed audits observed leaked temporary roots, port/sandbox sensitivity, skipped embedded PostgreSQL cases and macOS path failures.
units.designRationale: Keep test configuration minimal and rely on per-test setup/default discovery.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs reliable unit/integration/E2E tiers with resource isolation, deterministic profiles, coverage of critical boundaries and explicit skip/leak governance.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT as a production quality gate. Define separate projects for pure units, database/integration and browser E2E, with coverage/risk gates, fixtures, leak checks and CI platform matrix.
units.responsibilityConflict: Insufficient test governance weakens evidence for approval, identity and data-isolation guarantees.
evidence: Completed CLI audit evidence includes embedded PostgreSQL skips, sandbox port exhaustion, temp-root leakage and macOS canonical-path failures
units.securityFindings: No test-layer policy detects unclosed handles, filesystem/network leakage, unexpected live calls, skipped security suites or coverage regression. Defaults are not themselves a vulnerability, but they are insufficient evidence for this product's high-risk boundaries.
